methodological_rigor.justification: Development cohort of 1413 HR+/HER2- cases with 80/20 train-test split; external validation across 8 independent cohorts (n=1118). Ensemble machine learning approach with appropriate cross-validation (5-fold) and feature selection pipeline (random forest, Boruta, SHAP). Multiple statistical tests properly reported including multivariable Cox regression, restricted mean survival time analysis with Schoenfeld residuals checking. Limitations acknowledged: heterogeneous treatment regimens, batch effects corrected. No pre-registration mentioned or power calculation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Systematic review of multiple cohort studies (development + 8 external validation cohorts). Demonstrates robust prognostic validity for identifying HR+/HER2- patients at high recurrence risk independent of clinicopathological factors (HR 2.03, 95% CI 1.57-2.63, P<0.0001). Addresses unmet clinical need: identifies low-clinical-risk tumors at genomic high-risk for late recurrences, informs CDK4/6i treatment decisions. Shows clinical utility in node-negative and grade 1-2 tumors.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods section detailing feature selection pipeline, model architectures (SVM, gradient boosting), hyperparameter tuning via Bayesian search, normalization procedures. References to publicly available cohorts (cBioPortal, GEO, MetaGxBreast). Acknowledges limitations regarding treatment heterogeneity and missing clinical variables (menopausal status). No explicit data availability or code sharing statement; methods sufficient for general replication but not for exact computational reproduction.

novelty_literature.justification: Applies machine learning to existing challenge of breast cancer risk stratification; 14-gene signature novel but builds on established approach using ensemble methods. Primary contribution is demonstrating superior performance vs. Oncotype DX and EndoPredict in detecting late recurrences (>5 years), which is incremental. CDK4/6i interaction analyses exploratory with small sample sizes (n=85 metastatic). Meaningful but not breakthrough contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear methods, comprehensive results section showing development, internal validation, external validation stratified by clinical subgroups. Figures 1-4 effectively communicate model performance, benchmarking comparisons, and molecular underpinnings. Discussion appropriately addresses limitations including treatment heterogeneity, small drug sensitivity sample sizes, and need for prospective validation. Publication-ready quality with appropriate scientific rigor.

key_strengths: Robust external validation across 8 independent cohorts (n=1118) with consistent prognostic signal even in node-negative and low-grade tumors typically excluded from treatment escalation
Only assay demonstrated ability to predict late recurrences beyond 5 years when compared head-to-head with Oncotype DX and EndoPredict, addressing clinical gap noted in MINDACT/NATALEE trials
Ensemble machine learning approach with rigorous feature selection (random forest, Boruta, SHAP) and appropriate statistical handling (5-fold cross-validation, Schoenfeld residuals)
Comprehensive benchmarking multivariable analysis showing ER-Predict outperforms standard multigene panels when all three assays included in same model
key_concerns: Recomputed multigene panels (EndoPredict, Oncotype DX) not formally validated; comparison results may not reflect current clinical implementations
External validation cohorts heterogeneous in treatment (only 30.7% received endocrine therapy alone); limits ability to isolate biological vs. treatment-driven findings
Small sample size for drug sensitivity analysis (n=5 cell lines, n=85 metastatic patients treated with CDK4/6i); interaction with CDK4/6i therapy preliminary and exploratory
No data availability statement or code sharing commitment; missing menopausal status in most external cohort limits stratified validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper demonstrates solid methodological approach with meaningful external validation and clear clinical utility for late recurrence prediction. However, requires prospective validation and comparison to original (not recomputed) clinical assays before definitive superiority claims. Appropriate for high-impact specialized journals (Cancer Research, JCO Precision Oncology).
